<!-- introduction.md -->

# Introduction

raydom is a retained-mode UI tree for [raylib](https://www.raylib.com/). An application builds a tree of nodes,
assigns CSS-like styles, and attaches event listeners. raydom computes layout with flexbox and grid, shapes and wraps
text, routes pointer and keyboard input, and draws the result with raylib. The core is C23; a header-only C++20 layer
wraps it. Applications link it statically and ship as one binary.

This book documents the version shown in the version menu. Each release tag has its own copy of the book, so the
pages you read match the headers you compile against.

## Model

- **Context.** `rd_ctx` owns every node, style, class, font and listener. Destroying it frees all of them.
- **Nodes.** `rd_node` is a small value handle. A handle to a destroyed node is stale; every call on it is a no-op.
- **Styles.** A node's computed style merges defaults, inherited properties, classes, state variants, and the inline
  style, in that order.
- **Frame loop.** Each frame, `rd_update` feeds raylib's input and lays the tree out at the window size, and `rd_draw`
  draws it.

## How to read this book

[Getting started](getting-started/installation.md) covers installation and a first window. The
[guide](guide/tree.md) has one chapter per subsystem. The [reference](reference/properties.md) lists every
style property with its type, default and inheritance.

Every code sample in this book is a fragment of a program under `docs/examples/` in the repository. Those programs
are compiled by the test suite, and the ones that don't open a window run as tests, so the samples compile and
behave as described for this version.

Agents and tools can read the book as plain Markdown; see [For AI agents](agents.md).


<!-- getting-started/installation.md -->

# Installation

## Requirements

- CMake 3.25 or newer.
- A C23 compiler for C code that includes raydom (clang 18+, GCC 13+). A C++20 compiler for the C++ layer.
- raylib 6.0. raydom downloads it when the project doesn't provide one.

## FetchContent

```cmake
include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(raydom
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/ellimist-dev/raydom.git
    GIT_TAG        v0.1.1)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(raydom)

target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE raydom::raydom)
```

Link `raydom::extras` instead to get the [network view](../extras/graph.md); it links `raydom::raydom` for you.

raylib is resolved in this order: an existing `raylib` target in the project, an installed raylib found with
`find_package`, then a download. Set `RAYDOM_FETCH_RAYLIB=OFF` to require one of the first two.

## Installed package

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DRAYDOM_INSTALL=ON
cmake --build build
cmake --install build --prefix /your/prefix
```

```cmake
find_package(raydom 0.1 CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE raydom::raydom)
```

The package's version check accepts any patch release of the requested minor version while raydom is below 1.0.
After 1.0 it accepts any later release with the same major version.

## Options

| Option                  | Default        | Effect                                       |
| ----------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `RAYDOM_BUILD_EXTRAS`   | `ON`           | Build `raydom::extras`                       |
| `RAYDOM_FETCH_RAYLIB`   | `ON`           | Download raylib when it can't be found       |
| `RAYDOM_INSTALL`        | top-level only | Generate install rules and the CMake package |
| `RAYDOM_BUILD_TESTS`    | top-level only | Build the test suite                         |
| `RAYDOM_BUILD_EXAMPLES` | top-level only | Build the examples                           |
| `RAYDOM_SANITIZE`       | `OFF`          | Build with AddressSanitizer and UBSan        |

## Headers

| Header                         | Contents                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `<raydom/raydom.h>`            | The whole C API                            |
| `<raydom/raydom.hh>`           | The C++ layer; includes the C API          |
| `<raydom/extras/graph.h>`      | Network view, C                            |
| `<raydom/extras/graph.hh>`     | Network view, C++                          |
| `<raydom/role.h>`              | Roles and the button, text and input constructors |
| `<raydom/version.h>`           | `RD_VERSION_MAJOR`, `_MINOR`, `_PATCH` |


<!-- getting-started/quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

raydom has no built-in font. Load a TrueType or OpenType file before creating text; the first font loaded becomes
the default for every node.

## C

```c
#include <raydom/raydom.h>
#include <raylib.h>

int main(void) {
  SetConfigFlags(FLAG_WINDOW_HIGHDPI | FLAG_WINDOW_RESIZABLE);
  InitWindow(800, 600, "hello");
  rd_ctx* ctx = rd_ctx_create();
  rd_font_load_file(ctx, FONT_PATH);  // any .ttf or .otf file

  rd_node card = rd_node_create_text(ctx, "Hello from raydom", RD_TEXT_NUL);
  rd_node_set_style(ctx, card,
                    &(rd_style){
                        .padding       = rd_edges_all(rd_px(16)),
                        .border_radius = rd_corners_all(rd_px(8)),
                        .background    = rd_hex(0x1a1f2b),
                        .color         = rd_hex(0xe4e7ee),
                    });
  rd_node_append(ctx, rd_ctx_root(ctx), card);

  while (!WindowShouldClose()) {
    rd_update(ctx);  // input, then layout at the window size
    BeginDrawing();
    ClearBackground(BLACK);
    rd_draw(ctx);
    EndDrawing();
  }
  rd_ctx_destroy(ctx);  // before CloseWindow, so GPU resources are released
  CloseWindow();
}
```

## C++

```cpp
#include <raydom/raydom.hh>
#include <raylib.h>

#include <string>

using namespace rd::literals;

int main() {
  SetConfigFlags(FLAG_WINDOW_HIGHDPI | FLAG_WINDOW_RESIZABLE);
  InitWindow(800, 600, "hello");
  {
    rd::Context ctx;
    ctx.load_font_file(FONT_PATH);  // any .ttf or .otf file

    rd::Class button_style = ctx.create_class(rd::Style()
                                                  .padding(8_px, 16_px)
                                                  .border_radius(8_px)
                                                  .background(rd::hex(0x5b8cff))
                                                  .color(rd::hex(0xffffff)));
    button_style.on(RD_STATE_HOVER, rd::Style().background(rd::hex(0x7aa2ff)));

    int      clicks = 0;
    rd::Node label  = ctx.create_text("Clicked 0 times", rd::Style().color(rd::hex(0xe4e7ee)));
    rd::Node button = ctx.create_button("Click me").add_class(button_style);  // Tab focuses it; Enter and Space click it
    button.on_click([&] { label.text("Clicked " + std::to_string(++clicks) + " times"); });

    ctx.root()
        .style(rd::Style().padding(24_px).row_gap(12_px).align_items(RD_ALIGN_START))
        .append(button)
        .append(label);

    while (!WindowShouldClose()) {
      ctx.update();
      BeginDrawing();
      ClearBackground(BLACK);
      ctx.draw();
      EndDrawing();
    }
  }  // the context is destroyed here, before CloseWindow
  CloseWindow();
}
```

The C++ context is an RAII owner. It is scoped inside a block so it is destroyed before `CloseWindow`; raydom owns
GPU textures and a shader that must be released while the window still exists.

## Build

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(hello LANGUAGES C CXX)

include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(raydom
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/ellimist-dev/raydom.git
    GIT_TAG        v0.1.1)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(raydom)

add_executable(hello main.cc)
target_link_libraries(hello PRIVATE raydom::raydom)
target_compile_definitions(hello PRIVATE FONT_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/font.ttf")
```

For a single binary with no files next to it, embed the font and use `rd_font_load(ctx, data, size, false)`. With
C23 `#embed`:

```c
static const unsigned char font_data[] = {
#embed "font.ttf"
};
rd_font_load(ctx, font_data, sizeof font_data, false);  // false: the data outlives the context
```


<!-- getting-started/frame-loop.md -->

# The frame loop

```c
while (!WindowShouldClose()) {
  rd_update(ctx);
  BeginDrawing();
  ClearBackground(BLACK);
  rd_draw(ctx);
  EndDrawing();
}
```

`rd_update` does four things, in order:

1. Sets the context clock from `GetTime()` (`rd_ctx_set_time`).
2. Feeds raylib's keyboard and text input (`rd_ctx_key`, `rd_ctx_text`).
3. Feeds the mouse position, buttons and wheel (`rd_ctx_pointer`). Listeners run here.
4. Lays the tree out at the screen size (`rd_ctx_layout`).

`rd_draw` builds a display list from the laid-out tree and executes it with raylib. It must be called between
`BeginDrawing` and `EndDrawing`. Anything drawn with raylib after `rd_draw` appears on top of the UI.

## Mutating the tree

Tree and style changes are allowed at any time: in listeners, between frames, or from application logic. They are
recorded as dirty flags; nothing is recomputed until the next layout. Several changes in one frame cost one layout.

Geometry queries such as `rd_node_rect` return the result of the most recent layout. After changing the tree outside
the frame loop, call `rd_ctx_layout` before reading geometry.

## Without raylib input

`rd_update` is a convenience. Applications with their own input handling, and tests, call the lower-level functions
directly:

```c
rd_ctx_set_time(ctx, seconds);
rd_ctx_pointer(ctx, x, y, RD_BUTTON_PRIMARY, 0, 0);  // position, held buttons, wheel
rd_ctx_key(ctx, RD_KEY_TAB, true, false, 0);          // key, down, repeat, modifiers
rd_ctx_text(ctx, 'a');                                // one codepoint
rd_ctx_layout(ctx, width, height);
```

Nothing except `rd_update`, `rd_draw`, and paint callbacks touches raylib, so a context can be built, laid out and
driven with input without a window. The headless examples behind the guide chapters run this way.

## Lifetime

Destroy the context before `CloseWindow`. `rd_ctx_destroy` frees every node and runs every destroy callback
registered for userdata, listeners, measure and paint functions.


<!-- guide/tree.md -->

# Nodes and the tree

A context starts with one node, the root, which is sized to the layout viewport. Every other node is created
detached and becomes visible when it is attached under the root.

```c
rd_ctx* ctx  = rd_ctx_create();
rd_node root = rd_ctx_root(ctx);

rd_node list = rd_node_create(ctx);
rd_node a = rd_node_create(ctx), b = rd_node_create(ctx), c = rd_node_create(ctx);
rd_node_append(ctx, root, list);
rd_node_append(ctx, list, a);
rd_node_append(ctx, list, c);
rd_node_insert_before(ctx, list, b, c);  // list: a, b, c
```

## Handles

`rd_node` is `{index, gen}`. The context stores nodes in a slot array; `index` names a slot and `gen` counts how
many times that slot has been reused. Destroying a node bumps its slot's generation, so old handles stop matching.

Consequences:

- Handles are plain values. Copy them, store them in structs, compare them with `rd_node_eq`.
- A stale handle is safe. Every function checks it and returns `false`, a null node, or does nothing.
- `rd_node_is_null` tests for the zero handle, which functions return on failure. It doesn't test liveness; use
  `rd_node_alive` for that.

## Walking

```c
for (rd_node n = rd_node_first_child(ctx, list); !rd_node_is_null(n); n = rd_node_next_sibling(ctx, n)) {
  // visit n
}
```

C++ offers `for (rd::Node child : node.children())`. Neither form is stable if the loop body adds or removes siblings
of the node being visited; collect the nodes first in that case.

## Moving and detaching

```c
rd_node_append(ctx, root, b);  // moving: b leaves list and becomes root's last child
rd_node_detach(ctx, c);        // c stays alive, owned by the context, outside the tree
rd_node_append(ctx, list, c);  // and can be attached again later
```

`rd_node_append` and `rd_node_insert_before` move a node that already has a parent. They fail, returning `false`,
when the move would create a cycle, or when either handle is stale. A detached node keeps its subtree, styles and
listeners. It isn't laid out, drawn or hit-tested.

## Userdata

Each node carries one `void*` and an optional destroy callback that runs when the node is destroyed or the userdata
is replaced.

```c
typedef struct item {
  int id;
} item;

static void free_item(void* data) { free(data); }
```

```c
item* data = malloc(sizeof *data);
data->id   = 7;
rd_node_set_userdata(ctx, a, data, free_item);
item* back = rd_node_userdata(ctx, a);
```

C++: `node.emplace_userdata<T>(args...)` allocates a `T` owned by the node, and `node.userdata<T>()` returns it.

## Destroying

```c
rd_node_destroy(ctx, list);         // destroys list, a and c; a's userdata is freed
bool alive = rd_node_alive(ctx, a);  // false: the handle is stale, and every call on it is a no-op
```

`rd_node_destroy` destroys the subtree, depth first, and runs its destroy callbacks. The root can't be destroyed.
Destroying a node from inside one of its own listeners is allowed; see [Events](events.md#mutating-during-dispatch).


<!-- guide/styles.md -->

# Styles and classes

`rd_style` is a struct with one field per property. Every field type reserves zero for "unset", so a
compound literal names only the properties it sets. The [property reference](../reference/properties.md) lists them
all.

## Inline styles

```c
rd_node_set_style(ctx, node,
                  &(rd_style){
                      .width         = rd_px(240),
                      .padding       = rd_edges_vh(rd_px(8), rd_px(12)),  // vertical, horizontal
                      .border_width  = rd_edges_all(rd_px(1)),
                      .border_color  = rd_hex(0x272d3a),
                      .border_radius = rd_corners_all(rd_px(6)),
                      .background    = rd_hex(0x1a1f2b),
                  });
rd_node_merge_style(ctx, node, &(rd_style){.padding.left = rd_px(20)});  // only the left side changes
```

`rd_node_set_style` replaces the inline style. `rd_node_merge_style` copies the set fields over it and leaves the
rest. Passing `NULL` to `rd_node_set_style` clears it.

Value constructors: `rd_px`, `rd_pct`, `rd_num`, `rd_fr`, `rd_auto()`, `rd_min_content()`, `rd_max_content()`.
Colors: `rd_hex(0xRRGGBB)`, `rd_rgb`, `rd_rgba`. Box sides: `rd_edges_all`, `rd_edges_vh`, or designated
`.padding.left`. See [Values and units](../reference/values.md).

## Classes

A class is a reusable style with optional variants per state. Classes live until the context is destroyed;
`rd_class_set` replaces a class's base style and restyles every node that uses it.

```c
rd_class button_style = rd_class_create(ctx, &(rd_style){.padding    = rd_edges_vh(rd_px(6), rd_px(14)),
                                                        .background = rd_hex(0x1d2230)});
rd_class primary      = rd_class_create(ctx, &(rd_style){.background = rd_hex(0x5b8cff)});
rd_class_set_state(ctx, button_style, RD_STATE_HOVER, &(rd_style){.background = rd_hex(0x252c3d)});
rd_class_set_state(ctx, button_style, RD_STATE_DISABLED, &(rd_style){.opacity = rd_num(0.4f)});

rd_node ok = rd_node_create(ctx);
rd_node_append(ctx, root, ok);
rd_node_add_class(ctx, ok, button_style);
rd_node_add_class(ctx, ok, primary);  // later classes win: the background is primary's
```

```c
const rd_style* s = rd_node_computed_style(ctx, ok);
// background from primary (the later class), padding from button_style (primary doesn't set it)
```

## Precedence

For each property, the last of these that sets it wins:

1. Defaults (the reference's Default column).
2. The parent's computed value, for inherited properties.
3. Class base styles, in the order the classes were added.
4. Class state variants for the node's current states, ordered by state: `hover`, `focus_within`, `focus`,
   `focus_visible`, `active`, `disabled`. Within one state, later classes win.
5. The inline style.

Inline styles beat every class and every state variant. Put anything that should change on hover in a class, not
inline.

## States

raydom sets `hover`, `active`, `focus`, `focus_visible` and `focus_within` from input. `disabled` is set only by the
application.

```c
rd_node_set_states(ctx, ok, RD_STATE_HOVER, true);
// the hover variant of button_style now beats primary's base background
```

A disabled node and its descendants receive no pointer down, up or click events and can't be focused. Hover and
pointer move still apply.

`focus_visible` is set when focus came from the keyboard, or when the focused node is a text input. Use it, not
`focus`, for focus rings.

## Inheritance

```c
rd_node child = rd_node_create(ctx);
rd_node_append(ctx, node, child);
rd_node_merge_style(ctx, node, &(rd_style){.color = rd_hex(0xe4e7ee), .font_size = rd_px(18)});
// child's computed color and font_size come from node; its background doesn't
```

Inherited properties: `color`, `font`, `font_size`, `line_height`, `white_space`, `user_select`, `pointer_events`,
`caret_color`, `selection_color`, `text_align`. The rest start from the default on every node.

## Computed styles

`rd_node_computed_style` returns the fully resolved style, with every field set. It computes styles if they are
dirty. The pointer is valid until the next node is created.


<!-- guide/layout.md -->

# Layout

Every node is a flex container by default, with `flex_direction: column`, `align_items: stretch`, and
`flex_shrink: 0`. Children stack vertically and fill the width. Set `display` to `RD_DISPLAY_GRID` for grid, or
`RD_DISPLAY_NONE` to remove a node from layout, drawing and hit-testing.

Sizes are border-box: `width` includes padding and border.

## Flexbox

```c
// A toolbar: fixed-width side items and a flexible middle.
rd_node bar = add(ctx, root,
                  (rd_style){.flex_direction = RD_FLEX_ROW,
                             .align_items    = RD_ALIGN_CENTER,
                             .column_gap     = rd_px(8),
                             .padding        = rd_edges_all(rd_px(8)),
                             .height         = rd_px(48)});
rd_node left   = add(ctx, bar, (rd_style){.width = rd_px(80), .height = rd_px(32)});
rd_node middle = add(ctx, bar, (rd_style){.flex_grow = rd_num(1), .flex_basis = rd_px(0), .height = rd_px(32)});
rd_node right  = add(ctx, bar, (rd_style){.width = rd_px(80), .height = rd_px(32)});
```

The algorithm follows [CSS Flexible Box Layout §9](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-flexbox-1/#layout-algorithm), with
these differences:

- `flex_shrink` defaults to 0. Items keep their size and overflow unless they opt in to shrinking.
- `flex_direction` defaults to column.
- `min_width` and `min_height` `auto` resolve to 0, not to the content size. An item is never smaller than its
  padding plus border.

`flex_basis: 0` with `flex_grow: 1` splits free space without regard to content, which is the common "fill the rest"
pattern.

## Grid

```c
rd_track  cols[3] = {rd_track_of(rd_px(200)), rd_track_of(rd_fr(1)), rd_track_of(rd_fr(2))};
rd_node   grid    = add(ctx, root,
                        (rd_style){.display               = RD_DISPLAY_GRID,
                                   .grid_template_columns = rd_tracks_create(ctx, cols, 3),
                                   .grid_auto_rows        = rd_track_of(rd_px(40)),
                                   .column_gap            = rd_px(10),
                                   .row_gap               = rd_px(10)});
rd_node header = add(ctx, grid, (rd_style){.grid_column_start = rd_line(1), .grid_column_end = rd_line(-1)});
for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) add(ctx, grid, (rd_style){0});  // auto-placed, row by row
```

Track lists are interned: `rd_tracks_create` copies the array into the context and returns a handle that styles
refer to. The list lives until the context is destroyed. C++ builds them with
`ctx.tracks({200_px, 1_fr, 2_fr})` and `rd::repeat(3, {1_fr})`.

A track is `{min, max}`. `rd_track_of(v)` uses `v` for both, except `fr`, which becomes `minmax(auto, fr)` as in
CSS. `rd_track_minmax` builds any other pair.

Placement uses `grid_{column,row}_{start,end}`: `rd_line(n)` is a 1-based line, negative from the end of the
explicit grid; `rd_span(n)` spans tracks. Items without placement are auto-placed in `grid_auto_flow` order into
implicit tracks sized by `grid_auto_rows` and `grid_auto_columns`.

The algorithm follows [CSS Grid §11](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-1/#layout-algorithm). Named lines, named areas
and `dense` packing are not implemented.

## Running layout and reading geometry

```c
rd_ctx_layout(ctx, 800, 600);  // rd_update does this for you in a raylib app
rd_rect m = rd_node_rect(ctx, middle);    // relative to the parent's border box
rd_rect h = rd_node_bounds(ctx, header);  // relative to the root, after scrolling
```

| Function               | Returns                                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rd_node_rect`         | Border box relative to the parent's border box, before scroll |
| `rd_node_bounds`       | Border box in root coordinates, after scroll offsets           |
| `rd_node_box`          | Resolved margin, border and padding insets                     |
| `rd_node_content_size` | Extent of the padding box and children's margin boxes          |
| `rd_node_baseline`     | First baseline from the top of the border box, or NaN          |

Layout results are cached per node and reused when neither the node nor its inputs changed.

## Absolute positioning

```c
rd_node badge = add(ctx, bar,
                    (rd_style){.position = RD_POSITION_ABSOLUTE,
                               .inset    = {.top = rd_px(-6), .right = rd_px(-6)},
                               .width    = rd_px(12),
                               .height   = rd_px(12)});
```

An absolute node is positioned against its parent's padding box using `inset`. With both insets on an axis and
no size, it stretches between them. It takes no space in the parent's
flex or grid layout.

## Scrolling

```c
rd_node list = add(ctx, root, (rd_style){.height = rd_px(200), .overflow_y = RD_OVERFLOW_SCROLL});
for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) add(ctx, list, (rd_style){.height = rd_px(24)});
rd_ctx_layout(ctx, 800, 600);
rd_node_set_scroll(ctx, list, 0, 300);  // clamped to the content: at most 50 * 24 - 200
```

`overflow_x` and `overflow_y` set to `RD_OVERFLOW_HIDDEN` clip children; `RD_OVERFLOW_SCROLL` also makes the node
scroll with the wheel. The wheel scrolls the nearest scroll container under the pointer that can move in the gesture's
direction; once a gesture starts, it stays with that container until the wheel pauses.

## Custom measurement

A leaf node can report its own size with `rd_node_set_measure`. The callback receives a width and height, each with
a mode:

| Mode                     | Meaning                                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `RD_MEASURE_EXACTLY`     | The size is fixed; return it                  |
| `RD_MEASURE_AT_MOST`     | Return any size up to the value               |
| `RD_MEASURE_UNDEFINED`   | Size freely (max-content); the value is NaN   |
| `RD_MEASURE_MIN_CONTENT` | Return the smallest size without overflow; NaN |

Sizes are content-box. The callback must not change the tree. When the content it measures changes, call
`rd_node_mark_layout_dirty`.


<!-- guide/text.md -->

# Text and fonts

## Fonts

```c
rd_font body = rd_font_load_file(ctx, FONT_PATH);  // the first font loaded is the default
rd_font mono = rd_font_load_file(ctx, FONT_PATH);  // stands in for a second font file
if (body.id == 0) return 1;                        // a null handle means the file couldn't be loaded

rd_node code = rd_node_create(ctx);
rd_node_set_style(ctx, code, &(rd_style){.font = mono, .font_size = rd_px(13)});  // inherited by the text inside
rd_node_append(ctx, root, code);
```

`rd_font_load` takes TrueType or OpenType data in memory. With `copy = false` the data must outlive the context;
with `true` raydom copies it. `rd_font_load_file` reads and copies a file. Both return a null handle (`id == 0`) on
failure. The first font loaded becomes the default; `rd_ctx_set_default_font` changes it. In a style,
`(rd_font){0, true}` means "the default font".

`font` and `font_size` are inherited, so setting them on a container applies them to all the text inside it.
Glyphs are rasterized on demand into an atlas per font size and display scale.

## Text nodes

```c
rd_node para = add_text(ctx, root, (rd_style){.color = rd_hex(0xe4e7ee), .line_height = rd_num(1.4f)},
                        "Text wraps on spaces to the width its container gives it.");
rd_node_set_text(ctx, para, "New text; the next layout re-measures it.", RD_TEXT_NUL);
size_t      len;
const char* now = rd_node_text(ctx, para, &len);
```

`rd_node_set_text` makes the node a text leaf and copies the UTF-8 string. Pass a length, or `RD_TEXT_NUL` for a
NUL-terminated string. A text node's size comes from its text; it lays out no children. `rd_node_text` returns the
stored text, or `NULL` for a node that isn't a text leaf.

`line_height` accepts `rd_num` (a multiple of `font_size`), `rd_px`, or `rd_pct` (of `font_size`).

## Wrapping and overflow

```c
rd_node log_line = add_text(ctx, root,
                            (rd_style){.white_space   = RD_WHITE_SPACE_NOWRAP,
                                       .text_overflow = RD_TEXT_OVERFLOW_ELLIPSIS},
                            "a single long line that is cut with an ellipsis when it doesn't fit");
rd_node summary  = add_text(ctx, root,
                            (rd_style){.line_clamp    = rd_num(3),
                                       .text_overflow = RD_TEXT_OVERFLOW_ELLIPSIS},
                            "A paragraph that shows at most three lines and ends the third with an ellipsis.");
```

| `white_space` | Spaces and newlines | Wraps |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----- |
| `NORMAL`      | Collapsed           | Yes   |
| `NOWRAP`      | Collapsed           | No    |
| `PRE`         | Preserved           | No    |
| `PRE_WRAP`    | Preserved           | Yes   |

Lines break at spaces, and between CJK characters. A word longer than the line isn't broken; it overflows, and
`text_overflow: ellipsis` cuts it. `text_overflow: ellipsis` replaces
the end of a line that doesn't fit with "…". With `line_clamp: n`, at most `n` lines are shown, and with ellipsis
the last shown line ends with "…" when text was cut.

`text_align` aligns each line within the node's content box: `START`, `CENTER` or `END`.

## Highlights

```c
rd_highlight marks[] = {
    {.start = 0, .end = 3, .background = rd_hex(0xffd84d), .color = rd_hex(0x15171c)},  // "New"
};
rd_node_set_highlights(ctx, para, marks, 1);
```

Highlights are byte ranges with a background and an optional text color (alpha 0 keeps the node's color). They are
copied, kept across `rd_node_set_text`, and clamped to the text when drawn. Passing `NULL, 0` clears them. Use them
for search results or syntax marks; the user's selection is separate.

## Measuring

```c
float           w = rd_font_measure(ctx, (rd_font){0, true}, 16, "Hello", RD_TEXT_NUL);  // default font
rd_font_metrics m = rd_font_get_metrics(ctx, body, 16);
```

`rd_font_measure` returns the advance width of one unwrapped line. `rd_font_get_metrics` returns ascent, descent
(positive, below the baseline) and line gap in pixels. Both work without layout.

## Selection

Dragging over text whose `user_select` is `auto` (the default) selects it across text nodes, in tree order. The
selection is also settable from code:

```c
rd_ctx_select(ctx, para, 0, para, 8);
char   buf[64];
size_t n = rd_ctx_selection_text(ctx, buf, sizeof buf);  // "New text"
```

Offsets are bytes. `rd_ctx_selection_text` writes the selected text, one line per text node, and returns its full
length, so a first call with `buf = NULL` sizes the buffer. `RD_EVENT_SELECTION_CHANGE` fires on the root when the
selection changes. Set `user_select: none` on buttons and labels that shouldn't start a selection.


<!-- guide/events.md -->

# Events

## Listeners

```cpp
item.on_click([&] { log.push_back("item"); });                                  // bubble phase, target
list.on(RD_EVENT_CLICK, [&](rd::Event&) { log.push_back("list bubble"); });     // after the target
list.on(RD_EVENT_CLICK, [&](rd::Event&) { log.push_back("list capture"); }, true);  // before the target
```

The C form is:

```c
rd_listener l = rd_node_on(ctx, node, RD_EVENT_CLICK, on_click, data, free_data, 0);  // or RD_LISTEN_CAPTURE
rd_node_off(ctx, l);                                                                   // runs free_data
```

`fn(ctx, ev, data)` receives the event. `destroy(data)` runs when the listener is removed, or when its node is
destroyed. C++ listeners take `rd::Event&` or nothing; the callable is owned by the listener.

## Propagation

Dispatch follows the DOM. The path from the root to the target is fixed when dispatch starts. Capture listeners run
from the root down to the target's parent, then the target's listeners run (its capture listeners
first), then bubble listeners run from the parent up to the root. `ev->phase` says which phase is running; `ev->current` is the node whose listener is running
and `ev->target` is the node the event is for.

| Call                                  | Effect                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rd_event_stop_propagation`           | Finish the current node's listeners, then stop                 |
| `rd_event_stop_immediate_propagation` | Stop now; later listeners on the same node don't run           |
| `rd_event_prevent_default`            | Skip raydom's default action (scroll, focus, editing, click)   |

```cpp
rd::Node row = ctx.create(rd::Style().height(30_px));
row.on_click([](rd::Event& e) {
  e.stop_propagation();       // no bubble listeners run; capture listeners already have
  e.current().destroy();      // safe during dispatch: freed when dispatch ends
});
list.append(row);
```

Stopping at the target doesn't undo capture listeners that already ran on ancestors.

## Event types

| Type                         | Target                     | Bubbles | Default action                     |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `POINTER_DOWN`, `_UP`, `_MOVE` | Node under the pointer, or the capturing node | Yes | Down: focus, start selection |
| `POINTER_ENTER`, `_LEAVE`    | Each node entered or left  | No      |                                    |
| `CLICK`                      | Common ancestor of the press and release targets | Yes | |
| `WHEEL`                      | Node under the pointer     | Yes     | Scroll the nearest scroll container |
| `KEY_DOWN`, `KEY_UP`         | Focused node, or the root  | Yes     | Down: Tab focus, Enter/Space click, editing |
| `TEXT`                       | Focused node, or the root  | Yes     | Insert into a focused input        |
| `FOCUS`, `BLUR`              | The node gaining or losing focus | No |                                  |
| `FOCUS_IN`, `FOCUS_OUT`      | Same                       | Yes     |                                    |
| `INPUT`                      | The input                  | Yes     |                                    |
| `CHANGE`                     | The input                  | Yes     |                                    |
| `SELECTION_CHANGE`           | The root                   | No      |                                    |

Event fields: `x`, `y` in root coordinates; `local_x`, `local_y` relative to `current`'s border box; `wheel_x`,
`wheel_y` in notches; `button` (the button that changed) and `buttons` (held mask); `key`, `mods`, `repeat`;
`codepoint` for text; `related` for focus events.

`CLICK` fires for the primary button only.

## Pointer capture

```cpp
rd::Node handle = ctx.create(rd::Style().width(20_px).height(20_px));
float    dragged = 0;
handle.on(RD_EVENT_POINTER_DOWN, [](rd::Event& e) { e.current().capture_pointer(); });
handle.on(RD_EVENT_POINTER_MOVE, [&](rd::Event& e) {
  if (e.buttons() & RD_BUTTON_PRIMARY) dragged = e.local_x();  // keeps arriving outside the handle
});
```

While a node holds the capture, every pointer event goes to it, wherever the pointer is, until all buttons are
released or `rd_node_release_pointer_capture` is called. Use it for drags, sliders and splitters.

## Overriding defaults

```cpp
rd::Node canvas = ctx.create(rd::Style().height(100_px).overflow_y(RD_OVERFLOW_SCROLL));
canvas.on(RD_EVENT_WHEEL, [](rd::Event& e) { e.prevent_default(); });  // handle the wheel yourself, no scrolling
```

## Hit-testing

`rd_node_at(ctx, x, y)` returns the topmost node under a point after layout. Nodes with `pointer_events: none` are
skipped, and children inherit it unless they set `auto`. Use `none` for overlays and decorative layers that
shouldn't take the pointer.

## Mutating during dispatch

Listeners may create, move and destroy nodes, including the target and the current node. A node destroyed during
dispatch is detached at once and freed when dispatch ends, so `ev->current` stays valid until the listener returns.
A listener added to a node while that node's listeners are running doesn't run for the current event.


<!-- guide/input.md -->

# Focus, keyboard and text input

## Focus

A node can take focus when its `focusable` is `TAB` (pointer, code and Tab) or `POINTER` (pointer and code). Inputs
and nodes with an interactive [role](roles.md), such as buttons from `rd_node_create_button`, are focusable without
the style. Pressing the primary button focuses the target or its nearest focusable ancestor, and clears focus if there is
none. A listener that calls `rd_event_prevent_default` on `POINTER_DOWN` keeps focus where it was.

```cpp
rd::Class button_style = ctx.create_class(rd::Style().padding(6_px, 12_px));
button_style.on(RD_STATE_FOCUS_VISIBLE, rd::Style().box_shadow(0, 0, 0, rd::rgba(91, 140, 255, 200), 2));
rd::Node save  = ctx.create_button("Save").add_class(button_style);  // focusable by role
rd::Node badge = ctx.create(rd::Style().focusable(RD_FOCUSABLE_TAB));  // any node, by style
int      saves = 0;
save.on_click([&] { ++saves; });  // also fires on Enter or Space while focused
```

Tab and Shift+Tab move through `TAB` nodes in tree order, wrapping, skipping hidden and disabled subtrees.
`rd_node_focus(ctx, node)` focuses from code; a null node clears focus. `rd_ctx_focus_next` steps like Tab. A focus
change fires `BLUR`, `FOCUS_OUT`, `FOCUS`, `FOCUS_IN`, in that order.

Enter and Space on a focused node that isn't an input fire `CLICK`, so keyboard users can activate buttons without
extra code.

## Keyboard

```cpp
ctx.root().on(RD_EVENT_KEY_DOWN, [&](rd::Event& e) {
  if (e.key() == RD_KEY_ESCAPE) ctx.blur();
});
```

Keys go to the focused node, or the root when nothing has focus, and bubble. `ev->mods` is a mask of
`RD_MOD_SHIFT`, `RD_MOD_CTRL`, `RD_MOD_ALT`, `RD_MOD_SUPER`. Calling `rd_event_prevent_default` in a `KEY_DOWN`
listener suppresses Tab navigation, activation, and editing for that key.

## Text inputs

```cpp
rd::Node name  = ctx.create_input(false, rd::Style().width(240_px)).placeholder("Your name");
rd::Node notes = ctx.create_input(/*multiline=*/true, rd::Style().min_height(80_px));

std::string value;
name.on(RD_EVENT_INPUT, [&](rd::Event& e) { value = std::string(e.target().text()); });  // every edit
name.on(RD_EVENT_CHANGE, [&] { /* Enter, or leaving the field after editing */ });
```

`rd_node_create_input` creates an input, and `rd_node_make_input` turns an existing node into one: an editable text
leaf. A single-line input scrolls horizontally; a multi-line
input (`RD_INPUT_MULTILINE`) wraps and grows. `rd_node_text` reads the value and `rd_node_set_text` replaces it.
`rd_input_select` and `rd_input_selection` set and read the selection as byte offsets; the caret is the moving end.

`INPUT` fires after every edit. `CHANGE` fires when edits are committed: Enter in a single-line input, or blur after
an edit.

Editing keys, with Shortcut meaning Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, and Word meaning Option on macOS and Ctrl
elsewhere:

| Keys                        | Action                                  |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Arrows, Home, End           | Move; Shift extends the selection       |
| Word + Left/Right           | Move by word                            |
| Shortcut + Home/End         | Start or end of the value               |
| Backspace, Delete           | Delete; Word deletes a word; on macOS, Cmd deletes to the line edge |
| Shortcut + A                | Select all                              |
| Shortcut + C, X, V          | Copy, cut, paste                        |
| Shortcut + Z                | Undo; with Shift, redo                  |
| Shortcut + Y                | Redo                                    |
| Enter                       | Newline in multi-line; `CHANGE` in single-line |

Consecutive typed characters form one undo step.

## Clipboard

Inputs use an in-memory clipboard by default. `rd_update` installs raylib's system clipboard. Without raylib, provide
one:

```c
rd_ctx_set_clipboard(ctx, get_text, set_text, data);
```

## Driving input in tests

The C++ context has `press(key)` and `type(utf8)` helpers over `rd_ctx_key` and `rd_ctx_text`:

```cpp
ctx.press(RD_KEY_TAB);  // focus moves to the first focusable node: name
ctx.type("Ada");        // text events, one per codepoint
ctx.press(RD_KEY_TAB);  // notes
ctx.press(RD_KEY_TAB);  // save
ctx.press(RD_KEY_ENTER);
```


<!-- guide/roles.md -->

# Roles

A role says what a node is: a button, a heading, a text input. raydom doesn't draw or behave differently by role,
with one exception below. Roles exist so a future accessibility backend can describe the tree to screen readers
without every application revisiting its controls. Set them now and that work becomes a backend change only.

## Constructors

The direct way to get a role is to create the node with one:

| C                               | C++                              | Role                                  |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `rd_node_create_text(ctx, s, n)`| `ctx.create_text(s, style)`      | text                                  |
| `rd_node_create_button(ctx, s, n)` | `ctx.create_button(s, style)` | button, with a text label            |
| `rd_node_create_button(ctx, NULL, 0)` | `ctx.create_button(style)` | button, empty, for icon or composite content |
| `rd_node_create_input(ctx, flags)` | `ctx.create_input(multiline, style)` | text input or multi-line text input |

```cpp
#include <raydom/raydom.hh>
#include <raylib.h>

#include <string>

using namespace rd::literals;

int main() {
  SetConfigFlags(FLAG_WINDOW_HIGHDPI | FLAG_WINDOW_RESIZABLE);
  InitWindow(800, 600, "hello");
  {
    rd::Context ctx;
    ctx.load_font_file(FONT_PATH);  // any .ttf or .otf file

    rd::Class button_style = ctx.create_class(rd::Style()
                                                  .padding(8_px, 16_px)
                                                  .border_radius(8_px)
                                                  .background(rd::hex(0x5b8cff))
                                                  .color(rd::hex(0xffffff)));
    button_style.on(RD_STATE_HOVER, rd::Style().background(rd::hex(0x7aa2ff)));

    int      clicks = 0;
    rd::Node label  = ctx.create_text("Clicked 0 times", rd::Style().color(rd::hex(0xe4e7ee)));
    rd::Node button = ctx.create_button("Click me").add_class(button_style);  // Tab focuses it; Enter and Space click it
    button.on_click([&] { label.text("Clicked " + std::to_string(++clicks) + " times"); });

    ctx.root()
        .style(rd::Style().padding(24_px).row_gap(12_px).align_items(RD_ALIGN_START))
        .append(button)
        .append(label);

    while (!WindowShouldClose()) {
      ctx.update();
      BeginDrawing();
      ClearBackground(BLACK);
      ctx.draw();
      EndDrawing();
    }
  }  // the context is destroyed here, before CloseWindow
  CloseWindow();
}
```

Each returns a detached node, or a null node on allocation failure.

## Setting a role

```c
rd_node_set_role(ctx, title, RD_ROLE_HEADING);
rd_node_set_role(ctx, menu, RD_ROLE_LIST);
rd_role r = rd_node_role(ctx, node);
```

`RD_ROLE_AUTO`, the default, derives the role from the node: multi-line or single-line text input for inputs, text
for other text leaves, canvas for nodes with a paint callback, and generic otherwise. `rd_node_role` returns the
resolved role. Setting `RD_ROLE_AUTO` returns a node to its derived role.

The roles are a subset of [AccessKit](https://accesskit.dev/)'s: generic, group, button, link, checkbox, radio
button, text, label, heading, text input, multi-line text input, list, list item, image, canvas. More can be added
in a minor release.

## Focus

Interactive roles (button, link, checkbox, radio button) take focus without a `focusable` style, as inputs do:

- Tab reaches them, unless their `focusable` is `POINTER`, which keeps pointer focus and skips Tab.
- Enter and Space on a focused one fire `CLICK`, as for any focused node that isn't an input.
- To take one out of focus and pointer input, set `RD_STATE_DISABLED` on it.

Roles carry no other behavior. A checkbox doesn't toggle itself; the application tracks its state and styles it.


<!-- guide/canvas.md -->

# Canvases

A paint callback lets a node draw with raylib directly. The node is laid out and styled as usual; the callback draws
inside its content box.

```c
typedef struct chart {
  float values[5];
} chart;

static void paint_chart(rd_ctx* ctx, const rd_paint_info* info, void* data) {
  (void)ctx;
  const chart* c = data;
  rd_rect      r = info->content;  // screen coordinates, already scrolled
  rd_paint_scissor(info);          // clip to the visible part of the node
  float bar = r.width / 5;
  for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    float h = r.height * c->values[i];
    DrawRectangleRec((Rectangle){r.x + bar * (float)i + 4, r.y + r.height - h, bar - 8, h}, SKYBLUE);
  }
}
```

```c
static chart data = {{0.2f, 0.5f, 0.9f, 0.4f, 0.7f}};
rd_node      plot = rd_node_create(ctx);
rd_node_set_style(ctx, plot, &(rd_style){.height = rd_px(240), .margin = rd_edges_all(rd_px(20))});
rd_node_set_paint(ctx, plot, paint_chart, &data, NULL);  // NULL: nothing to free when the node goes away
rd_node_append(ctx, rd_ctx_root(ctx), plot);
```

The callback runs inside `rd_draw`, after the node's background and border and before its children, so children
draw on top. raydom flushes raylib's batch before the call, with no scissor or shader active.

`rd_paint_info` has:

| Field     | Meaning                                                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `content` | The node's content box in screen coordinates, after scrolling      |
| `clip`    | The part of the screen left visible by enclosing overflow containers |
| `dpi`     | Device pixels per logical pixel                                    |

`rd_paint_scissor(info)` clips raylib drawing to the content box within `clip`; raydom ends the scissor after the
callback. Restore any other raylib state you change. Rendering to a texture with `BeginTextureMode` inside the
callback is safe.

C++: `node.paint([](const rd_paint_info& info) { ... })`, with the callable owned by the node.

Pair a canvas with listeners on the same node for interaction: pointer events carry `local_x` and `local_y`
relative to the node's border box. Use the paint callback for drawing only; it must not change the tree.

The [network view](../extras/graph.md) is built on this.


<!-- cpp/overview.md -->

# The C++ layer

`<raydom/raydom.hh>` wraps the C API in namespace `rd`. It is header-only, needs C++20, and doesn't throw. Failures
are reported the same way as in C: null handles and `false`.

| C++               | C                    | Ownership                                     |
| ----------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `rd::Context`     | `rd_ctx*`            | Owns the context; move-only; destroys it      |
| `rd::Node`        | `rd_ctx*` + `rd_node`| Non-owning value, like the C handle           |
| `rd::Class`       | `rd_ctx*` + `rd_class` | Non-owning                                  |
| `rd::Style`       | `rd_style`           | Value; builder methods                        |
| `rd::Event`       | `rd_event*`          | Valid only inside the listener                |

`get()` and `handle()` return the C values, so C and C++ calls can be mixed freely on one context.

## Styles

`rd::Style` has one chainable setter per property, named as in the [reference](../reference/properties.md), plus
overloads for common shapes:

```cpp
using namespace rd::literals;

rd::Style()
    .padding(8_px, 16_px)                             // vertical, horizontal; also (all) and (t, r, b, l)
    .border_radius(6_px)                              // all corners
    .box_shadow(0, 4, 12, rd::rgba(0, 0, 0, 120))     // x, y, blur, color, spread = 0
    .grid_auto_rows(40_px)                            // any rd_val becomes a track
    .gap(8_px)                                        // row_gap and column_gap
    .flex(1);                                         // grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0
```

Literals: `_px`, `_pct`, `_fr`. Functions: `rd::px`, `rd::pct`, `rd::num`, `rd::fr`, `rd::hex`, `rd::rgb`,
`rd::rgba`, `rd::line`, `rd::span`, `rd::minmax`, `rd::repeat`. Constants: `rd::auto_`, `rd::min_content`,
`rd::max_content`. `-5_px` works for negative offsets.

## Callbacks

`node.on(type, f, capture)`, `node.on_click(f)`, `node.paint(f)` and `node.measure(f)` take any callable. The
callable is moved into a heap allocation owned by raydom and deleted when the listener is removed or the node is
destroyed. Captured references must outlive the node, or the listener must be removed first.

`node.emplace_userdata<T>(args...)` constructs a `T` owned by the node; `node.userdata<T>()` returns it.

## The quickstart, annotated

```cpp
#include <raydom/raydom.hh>
#include <raylib.h>

#include <string>

using namespace rd::literals;

int main() {
  SetConfigFlags(FLAG_WINDOW_HIGHDPI | FLAG_WINDOW_RESIZABLE);
  InitWindow(800, 600, "hello");
  {
    rd::Context ctx;
    ctx.load_font_file(FONT_PATH);  // any .ttf or .otf file

    rd::Class button_style = ctx.create_class(rd::Style()
                                                  .padding(8_px, 16_px)
                                                  .border_radius(8_px)
                                                  .background(rd::hex(0x5b8cff))
                                                  .color(rd::hex(0xffffff)));
    button_style.on(RD_STATE_HOVER, rd::Style().background(rd::hex(0x7aa2ff)));

    int      clicks = 0;
    rd::Node label  = ctx.create_text("Clicked 0 times", rd::Style().color(rd::hex(0xe4e7ee)));
    rd::Node button = ctx.create_button("Click me").add_class(button_style);  // Tab focuses it; Enter and Space click it
    button.on_click([&] { label.text("Clicked " + std::to_string(++clicks) + " times"); });

    ctx.root()
        .style(rd::Style().padding(24_px).row_gap(12_px).align_items(RD_ALIGN_START))
        .append(button)
        .append(label);

    while (!WindowShouldClose()) {
      ctx.update();
      BeginDrawing();
      ClearBackground(BLACK);
      ctx.draw();
      EndDrawing();
    }
  }  // the context is destroyed here, before CloseWindow
  CloseWindow();
}
```

- `button_style` is an `rd::Class`: a shared style, not a node. `button_style.on(RD_STATE_HOVER, ...)` is the C++
  form of `rd_class_set_state`.
- `create_text(s, style)` creates a text node. `create_button(s, style)` does the same with the button
  [role](../guide/roles.md), which makes it focusable and activatable with Enter and Space.
- `append` returns the parent, so a subtree builds in one expression.
- The lambda captures `label` by reference; both live in the same scope as the context.


<!-- extras/graph.md -->

# Network view

`raydom::extras` provides `rdx_graph`, a view of nodes and edges for simulators and tools: lit 3D spheres, straight
edges with optional arrows and labels, and messages drawn in flight. It is built on a [canvas](../guide/canvas.md)
and lives in its own library so the core stays free of widgets.

```cmake
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE raydom::extras)
```

```cpp
#include <raydom/extras/graph.hh>  // or graph.h for C
```

## Creating a view

```cpp
rd::Node   canvas = ctx.create(rd::Style().flex(1));
rdx::Graph graph  = rdx::Graph::create(canvas);
graph.background(rd::hex(0x0b0d12));
graph.label_class().set(rd::Style().font_size(12_px).color(rd::hex(0xe4e7ee)));
ctx.root().append(canvas);
```

`rdx_graph_create(ctx, host)` turns `host` into the view. The graph lives until the host node is destroyed; there is
no separate destroy call. Node labels are text nodes under the host, styled with the class returned by
`label_class()`.

## Nodes and edges

```cpp
std::vector<rdx_node> nodes;
for (const char* name : {"A", "B", "C", "D", "E"}) nodes.push_back(graph.add_node({0, 0}, rd::hex(0x6c7385), name));
graph.layout_circle(nodes, {0, 0}, 160);
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < nodes.size(); i++)
  graph.connect(nodes[i], nodes[(i + 1) % nodes.size()], {.color = rd::hex(0x2a3142), .width = 1.5f});
graph.fit(60);
```

Positions are world units on a plane, y down. `rdx_node` and `rdx_edge` are generational handles, like `rd_node`.
Removing a node removes its edges. `fit(padding)` frames every node; `view(center, zoom)` sets the camera.

Defaults: node radius 20 world units, edge width 2 screen pixels, message radius 6 world units.

## Interaction

Dragging the background pans, and the wheel zooms about the pointer, between 0.1x and 10x. With
`RDX_GRAPH_DRAG_NODES`, dragging a node moves it. `RDX_GRAPH_NO_GRID` hides the background grid.

```cpp
graph.on([&](rdx_graph_event ev, rdx_node n) {
  if (ev == RDX_EVENT_NODE_CLICK) graph.select(n);
});
```

| Event                   | When                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `RDX_EVENT_NODE_ENTER`  | Pointer moves onto a node                              |
| `RDX_EVENT_NODE_LEAVE`  | Pointer leaves a node                                  |
| `RDX_EVENT_NODE_CLICK`  | Press and release on the same node without dragging    |
| `RDX_EVENT_NODE_DRAG`   | A node moved, with `RDX_GRAPH_DRAG_NODES`              |
| `RDX_EVENT_VIEW`        | The view panned or zoomed                              |

## Messages

The graph has no clock. Each frame, pass the messages in flight with their progress from 0 (at `from`) to 1 (at
`to`); the call replaces the previous set.

```cpp
float progress = t - static_cast<float>(static_cast<int>(t));  // your simulation decides this
graph.messages({{nodes[0], nodes[1], progress, rd::hex(0x5b8cff), 6}});
```

The `network` example in the repository is a Paxos simulator built this way.


<!-- reference/properties.md -->

# Style properties

Every field of `rd_style`, generated from the `RD_STYLE_PROPS` X-macro in `include/raydom/style.h` and the defaults
in `src/style.c` at this version.

- **Default** is the value a node has when nothing sets the property and it isn't inherited.
- *inherited* properties take the parent's computed value when unset.
- *paint only* properties change drawing without triggering layout. All others trigger relayout when they change.

In C++, each property is a setter of the same name on `rd::Style`. Enumerated values are written in full in C, for
example `RD_DISPLAY_GRID`.

## Box model

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `display` | `FLEX` | Layout mode of the node's children; `NONE` removes the node from layout, drawing and hit-testing.<br>*[`rd_display`](#rd-display)* |
| `position` | `RELATIVE` | `ABSOLUTE` takes the node out of flow and places it against the parent's padding box with `inset`.<br>*[`rd_position`](#rd-position)* |
| `width` | `auto` | Border-box width.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `height` | `auto` | Border-box height.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `min_width` | `auto` | Lower bound on width. `auto` is 0.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `min_height` | `auto` | Lower bound on height. `auto` is 0.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `max_width` | `auto` | Upper bound on width. `auto` is none.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `max_height` | `auto` | Upper bound on height. `auto` is none.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `margin` | `0px` | Outer spacing. `auto` margins absorb free space in flex layout.<br>*`rd_edges`* |
| `padding` | `0px` | Inner spacing. Percentages resolve against the containing block's width.<br>*`rd_edges`* |
| `border_width` | `0px` | Border thickness per side, in pixels.<br>*`rd_edges`* |
| `inset` | `auto` | Offsets from the containing block for absolute nodes; relative offsets otherwise.<br>*`rd_edges`* |
| `overflow_x` | `VISIBLE` | `HIDDEN` clips children horizontally; `SCROLL` clips and scrolls.<br>*[`rd_overflow`](#rd-overflow)* |
| `overflow_y` | `VISIBLE` | `HIDDEN` clips children vertically; `SCROLL` clips and scrolls.<br>*[`rd_overflow`](#rd-overflow)* |

## Flexbox

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `flex_direction` | `COLUMN` | Main axis of a flex container.<br>*[`rd_flex_direction`](#rd-flex-direction)* |
| `flex_wrap` | `NOWRAP` | Whether flex items wrap onto several lines.<br>*[`rd_flex_wrap`](#rd-flex-wrap)* |
| `flex_grow` | `0` | Share of positive free space, as `rd_num`.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `flex_shrink` | `0` | Share of negative free space, weighted by basis, as `rd_num`. Default 0: items don't shrink.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `flex_basis` | `auto` | Main size before free space is distributed.<br>*`rd_val`* |

## Alignment and gaps

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `justify_content` | `NORMAL` | Distribution of items along the main axis (flex) or of tracks along the row axis (grid).<br>*[`rd_align`](#rd-align)* |
| `align_items` | `STRETCH` | Default cross-axis alignment of the children.<br>*[`rd_align`](#rd-align)* |
| `align_self` | `AUTO` | Cross-axis alignment of this item; `AUTO` uses the parent's `align_items`.<br>*[`rd_align`](#rd-align)* |
| `align_content` | `NORMAL` | Distribution of flex lines or grid rows along the cross axis.<br>*[`rd_align`](#rd-align)* |
| `justify_items` | `STRETCH` | Grid: default inline-axis alignment of items in their areas.<br>*[`rd_align`](#rd-align)* |
| `justify_self` | `AUTO` | Grid: inline-axis alignment of this item; `AUTO` uses the parent's `justify_items`.<br>*[`rd_align`](#rd-align)* |
| `row_gap` | `0px` | Space between rows, or between items in a column flex container.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `column_gap` | `0px` | Space between columns, or between items in a row flex container.<br>*`rd_val`* |

## Grid

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `grid_template_columns` | none | Explicit column tracks, from `rd_tracks_create`.<br>*`rd_tracks`* |
| `grid_template_rows` | none | Explicit row tracks, from `rd_tracks_create`.<br>*`rd_tracks`* |
| `grid_auto_columns` | `auto` | Size of implicitly created columns.<br>*`rd_track`* |
| `grid_auto_rows` | `auto` | Size of implicitly created rows.<br>*`rd_track`* |
| `grid_auto_flow` | `ROW` | Whether auto-placement fills rows or columns first.<br>*[`rd_grid_flow`](#rd-grid-flow)* |
| `grid_column_start` | `auto` | Start line or span of the item's columns.<br>*`rd_grid_line`* |
| `grid_column_end` | `auto` | End line or span of the item's columns.<br>*`rd_grid_line`* |
| `grid_row_start` | `auto` | Start line or span of the item's rows.<br>*`rd_grid_line`* |
| `grid_row_end` | `auto` | End line or span of the item's rows.<br>*`rd_grid_line`* |

## Paint

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `background` | transparent | Fill of the border box, inside the rounded corners.<br>*`rd_color`, paint only* |
| `border_color` | transparent | Color of the border.<br>*`rd_color`, paint only* |
| `border_radius` | `0px` | Corner radii.<br>*`rd_corners`, paint only* |
| `opacity` | `1` | Opacity of the node and its subtree, 0 to 1, as `rd_num`.<br>*`rd_val`, paint only* |
| `box_shadow` | none | Outer shadow: offset, blur, spread and color.<br>*`rd_shadow`, paint only* |

## Text

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `color` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 255)` | Text color.<br>*`rd_color`, inherited, paint only* |
| `font` | default font | Font handle from `rd_font_load`; `{0, true}` is the default font.<br>*`rd_font`, inherited* |
| `font_size` | `16px` | Text size in pixels.<br>*`rd_val`, inherited* |
| `line_height` | `1.2` | Line box height: `rd_num` times `font_size`, `rd_px`, or `rd_pct` of `font_size`.<br>*`rd_val`, inherited* |
| `white_space` | `NORMAL` | Collapsing of spaces and newlines, and whether lines wrap.<br>*[`rd_white_space`](#rd-white-space), inherited* |
| `text_overflow` | `CLIP` | Treatment of text cut by the box or by `line_clamp`.<br>*[`rd_text_overflow`](#rd-text-overflow), paint only* |
| `line_clamp` | `0` | Maximum number of lines shown, as `rd_num`; 0 is unlimited.<br>*`rd_val`* |
| `text_align` | `START` | Horizontal alignment of each line in the content box.<br>*[`rd_text_align`](#rd-text-align), inherited, paint only* |
| `user_select` | `AUTO` | Whether dragging over the text selects it.<br>*[`rd_user_select`](#rd-user-select), inherited, paint only* |
| `caret_color` | transparent | Input caret color; transparent uses `color`.<br>*`rd_color`, inherited, paint only* |
| `selection_color` | `rgba(91, 140, 255, 90)` | Background of selected text.<br>*`rd_color`, inherited, paint only* |

## Interaction

| Property | Default | Description |
| -------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `pointer_events` | `AUTO` | `NONE` makes the node invisible to hit-testing.<br>*[`rd_pointer_events`](#rd-pointer-events), inherited, paint only* |
| `focusable` | `NONE` | Whether the node takes focus, and whether Tab reaches it.<br>*[`rd_focusable`](#rd-focusable), paint only* |

## Enumerations

### rd_display

`RD_DISPLAY_*`: `FLEX`, `GRID`, `NONE`

### rd_position

`RD_POSITION_*`: `RELATIVE`, `ABSOLUTE`

### rd_overflow

`RD_OVERFLOW_*`: `VISIBLE`, `HIDDEN`, `SCROLL`

### rd_flex_direction

`RD_FLEX_*`: `ROW`, `COLUMN`, `ROW_REVERSE`, `COLUMN_REVERSE`

### rd_flex_wrap

`RD_FLEX_*`: `NOWRAP`, `WRAP`, `WRAP_REVERSE`

### rd_align

`RD_ALIGN_*`: `AUTO`, `NORMAL`, `START`, `END`, `CENTER`, `STRETCH`, `BASELINE`, `SPACE_BETWEEN`, `SPACE_AROUND`, `SPACE_EVENLY`

### rd_grid_flow

`RD_GRID_FLOW_*`: `ROW`, `COLUMN`

### rd_white_space

`RD_WHITE_SPACE_*`: `NORMAL`, `NOWRAP`, `PRE`, `PRE_WRAP`

### rd_text_overflow

`RD_TEXT_OVERFLOW_*`: `CLIP`, `ELLIPSIS`

### rd_text_align

`RD_TEXT_ALIGN_*`: `START`, `CENTER`, `END`

### rd_user_select

`RD_USER_SELECT_*`: `AUTO`, `NONE`

### rd_pointer_events

`RD_POINTER_EVENTS_*`: `AUTO`, `NONE`

### rd_focusable

`RD_FOCUSABLE_*`: `NONE`, `TAB`, `POINTER`


<!-- reference/values.md -->

# Values and units

## Lengths: `rd_val`

| Constructor          | C++               | Meaning                                    |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `rd_px(v)`           | `v_px`            | Logical pixels                             |
| `rd_pct(v)`          | `v_pct`           | Percent of the containing block            |
| `rd_num(v)`          | `rd::num(v)`      | Unitless: flex factors, opacity, line height multiple, line clamp |
| `rd_fr(v)`           | `v_fr`            | Grid fraction of free space                |
| `rd_auto()`          | `rd::auto_`       | Automatic                                  |
| `rd_min_content()`   | `rd::min_content` | Grid tracks: smallest size without overflow |
| `rd_max_content()`   | `rd::max_content` | Grid tracks: size without wrapping          |

Percentages of width resolve against the containing block's width. Percentages of height resolve against its height
when that is definite, and are treated as `auto` otherwise. Padding and margin percentages resolve against the
width on every side, as in CSS.

Logical pixels are scaled by raylib's DPI scale when drawn; layout never sees device pixels.

## Colors: `rd_color`

`rd_hex(0xRRGGBB)` (opaque), `rd_rgb(r, g, b)`, `rd_rgba(r, g, b, a)`. A zero `rd_color` is unset. Transparent is
`rd_rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, which is set.

## Edges and corners

`rd_edges` is `{top, right, bottom, left}`; `rd_edges_all(v)` and `rd_edges_vh(vertical, horizontal)` build it.
`rd_corners` is `{top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left}`; `rd_corners_all(v)` builds it. Each side is an
independent `rd_val`, so `.padding.left = rd_px(4)` sets one side and leaves the others unset.

## Shadows

`rd_shadow` is `{x, y, blur, spread, color}`. `rd_shadow_of(x, y, blur, color)` builds one with zero spread.

## Grid

| Constructor                | Meaning                                       |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `rd_track_of(v)`           | A track sized `v`; `fr` becomes `minmax(auto, fr)` |
| `rd_track_minmax(min, max)`| A track between two sizes                     |
| `rd_tracks_create(ctx, a, n)` | Interns a track list; returns a handle     |
| `rd_tracks_none()`         | No explicit tracks                            |
| `rd_line(n)`               | A grid line, 1-based; negative from the end   |
| `rd_span(n)`               | Span `n` tracks                               |
| `rd_line_auto()`           | Auto placement                                |

## Unset

Zero means unset for every style type. That is what makes `&(rd_style){.width = rd_px(10)}` set only the width,
and it is why `rd_node_merge_style` can tell which fields to copy.


<!-- reference/limits.md -->

# Limits

What raydom doesn't do in this version. Behavior outside these limits is unspecified.

## Layout

- No `display: block` or `inline`; every container is flex or grid. Text nodes are leaves.
- Grid: no named lines, no named areas, no `dense` auto-flow, no `repeat(auto-fill)`.
- No `position: fixed` or `sticky`.
- No `z-index`; children draw in tree order, later siblings on top.
- No `aspect_ratio`, no `transform`.
- `min_width`/`min_height` `auto` is 0, not the content size.

## Text

- One font per text node. No rich text inside a node; use several text nodes in a row.
- No shaping: no ligatures, no contextual forms, no bidirectional text. Pair kerning from the font is applied. Latin, Cyrillic,
  Greek and CJK display; Arabic and Indic scripts don't shape correctly.
- No hyphenation. Words longer than the line overflow.
- No double- or triple-click word or line selection.

## Input

- No IME composition events. Text input is one codepoint at a time from raylib.
- No touch or gesture input beyond what raylib reports as the mouse.
- No accessibility tree.

## Rendering

- No images or textures as node backgrounds; use a canvas.
- Shadows are outer box shadows only.
- No gradients.

## Threads

A context is single-threaded. Separate contexts on separate threads don't share state, but raylib drawing must
happen on the thread that owns the window.


<!-- agents.md -->

# For AI agents

This page is for coding agents and the tools that feed them. It states the facts an agent needs to write correct
raydom code, in a form that is cheap to retrieve.

## Machine-readable copies

Every published version of this book has, next to its HTML:

| Path              | Contents                                                       |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `llms.txt`        | Index of pages with one-line descriptions, per [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/) |
| `llms-full.txt`   | The whole book as one Markdown file, code samples inlined      |
| `<page>.md`       | Each page as Markdown, at the HTML page's path with `.md`      |

Use the copy under the version that matches the project's `GIT_TAG` or `find_package` version, for example
`/v0.1.1/llms-full.txt`. `/latest/` follows the newest release; `/dev/` follows the main branch and may
describe unreleased API.

The headers are the ground truth. `include/raydom/*.h` documents every function in a comment above it, and
`include/raydom/style.h` defines every style property in the `RD_STYLE_PROPS` X-macro.

## Rules

1. Create the context after `InitWindow` and destroy it before `CloseWindow`. In C++, scope `rd::Context` in a block
   that ends before `CloseWindow`.
2. Load a font before creating text. There is no built-in font.
3. Call `rd_update` before `BeginDrawing` and `rd_draw` between `BeginDrawing` and `EndDrawing`, once per frame.
4. A new node is detached. Append it under `rd_ctx_root(ctx)` or a descendant, or it isn't drawn.
5. `rd_style` fields left out are unset, and unset fields fall through to classes, inheritance and defaults.
   Write `&(rd_style){.width = rd_px(100)}`. Never pass a computed style as an inline style: it sets every
   property and overrides all classes.
6. The default `flex_direction` is column and the default `flex_shrink` is 0. Set `flex_direction = RD_FLEX_ROW`
   for rows. Set `flex_shrink` explicitly if items must shrink.
7. Inline styles beat class state variants. Put hover, focus and active styling in classes.
8. Lengths need units: `rd_px(8)`, not `8`. Unitless values (`flex_grow`, `opacity`, `line_clamp`, multiplier
   `line_height`) use `rd_num`.
9. Grid track lists are handles: build them with `rd_tracks_create` (C) or `ctx.tracks({...})` (C++).
10. Handles are values. Store `rd_node`, not pointers. Check `rd_node_alive` when a node may have been destroyed.
11. Listeners may mutate and destroy nodes, including their own node. A destroyed node is freed when dispatch
    ends.
12. Geometry (`rd_node_rect`, `rd_node_bounds`) reflects the last layout. After building or changing the tree
    outside the frame loop, call `rd_ctx_layout` before reading it.
13. The C++ layer doesn't throw. Check returned handles and `bool` results where failure matters.
14. raydom doesn't own the main loop, the window, or time. The application drives all three.
15. Create controls with their role: `rd_node_create_button` / `ctx.create_button` for buttons, `rd_node_create_input`
    / `ctx.create_input` for inputs, `rd_node_set_role` for headings, lists, links and checkboxes. Don't build a
    button from a plain node and a click listener; it gets no role and no default focus.

## Minimal program

```c
#include <raydom/raydom.h>
#include <raylib.h>

int main(void) {
  SetConfigFlags(FLAG_WINDOW_HIGHDPI | FLAG_WINDOW_RESIZABLE);
  InitWindow(800, 600, "hello");
  rd_ctx* ctx = rd_ctx_create();
  rd_font_load_file(ctx, FONT_PATH);  // any .ttf or .otf file

  rd_node card = rd_node_create_text(ctx, "Hello from raydom", RD_TEXT_NUL);
  rd_node_set_style(ctx, card,
                    &(rd_style){
                        .padding       = rd_edges_all(rd_px(16)),
                        .border_radius = rd_corners_all(rd_px(8)),
                        .background    = rd_hex(0x1a1f2b),
                        .color         = rd_hex(0xe4e7ee),
                    });
  rd_node_append(ctx, rd_ctx_root(ctx), card);

  while (!WindowShouldClose()) {
    rd_update(ctx);  // input, then layout at the window size
    BeginDrawing();
    ClearBackground(BLACK);
    rd_draw(ctx);
    EndDrawing();
  }
  rd_ctx_destroy(ctx);  // before CloseWindow, so GPU resources are released
  CloseWindow();
}
```

## Verifying generated code

Headless programs can drive input and assert on results without a window; see
[The frame loop](getting-started/frame-loop.md#without-raylib-input). The repository's `docs/examples/` holds
programs of this kind for each chapter.


<!-- versioning.md -->

# Versioning

raydom follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/). Before 1.0, a minor release may break the API; a patch
release doesn't. From 1.0, only a major release may break it.

## Documentation versions

Every release tag publishes its own copy of this book, built from the sources at that tag, under `/<tag>/`. A
published copy is never rebuilt by later releases, so it keeps describing the version it was built from. The
version menu in the top bar switches between them and keeps the current page when it exists in the target version.

| Path        | Built from                     |
| ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| `/vX.Y.Z/`  | The tag `vX.Y.Z`               |
| `/latest/`  | The newest release tag         |
| `/dev/`     | The `main` branch              |

The book's code samples are compiled, and the headless ones run, by the test suite at each tag, so a version's
samples match that version's API.

## Checking a version in code

```c
#include <raydom/version.h>

#if RD_VERSION_MAJOR == 0 && RD_VERSION_MINOR < 2
// ...
#endif
```

`RD_VERSION_STRING` holds the full version.
